name: Chicago
title: Holidays in Chicago
intro: A shiny giant bean, Sue the T. rex and a glass ledge 103 floors up. Here's what Chicago is like with the family, when to go and how long to stay.
facts_note: Check entry rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: June to September is best, with lake beaches, festivals and outdoor concerts. Winter is bitterly cold and windy, though December has festive lights and ice skating.

things.name: Millennium Park
things.blurb: See yourself in the Bean and splash in the Crown Fountain in summer.

things.name: Field Museum
things.blurb: Sue, one of the most complete T. rex skeletons ever found.

things.name: Museum of Science and Industry
things.blurb: Climb inside a real German U-boat.

things.name: Lincoln Park Zoo
things.blurb: One of the last free zoos in the US.

things.name: Architecture river cruise
things.blurb: A boat tour between the skyscrapers.

things.name: Navy Pier
things.blurb: A giant Ferris wheel, a children's museum and fireworks in summer.

faqs.question: Is Chicago good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes, especially in summer. The museums are excellent, the lakefront has beaches and bike paths, and it's less hectic than New York.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need?
faqs.answer: Four or five nights covers the museums, the lakefront and a deep-dish pizza or two.

faqs.question: Do UK families need a visa?
faqs.answer: Most British passport holders, children included, apply for an ESTA online before they fly rather than a visa. Check GOV.UK for the current rules.

faqs.question: Can you swim in Lake Michigan?
faqs.answer: Yes, at the city beaches in summer, when lifeguards are on duty. The water stays cool.
